title: Run deleting old index gens after snapshot in the background

timeline.message:
Run deleting old index gens after snapshot in the background

There's no need to run the old index gens cleanup before completing a
snapshot operation (and starting the next operation).
This also makes it so the snapshot listener is resolved on the master
thread, so we can get a consistent view of the cluster state when
calling clusterService.state() in the callback. This fixes test failure
 #97572 which resulted from accessing the state on the `SNAPSHOT` pool
	after a master failover.

Fixes #97572
timeline.author: Armin Braun

timeline.body:
Bit of a strange way to deal with the test failure but I think this is a valid optimisation in isolation. I think it's fine to have that one tasks forked and executing without waiting for it to the snapshot pool. 

There's no need to run the old index gens cleanup before completing a snapshot operation (and starting the next operation). This also makes it so the snapshot listener is resolved on the master thread, so we can get a consistent view of the cluster state when calling clusterService.state() in the callback. This fixes test failure
#97572 which resulted from accessing the state on the `SNAPSHOT` pool after a master failover.

Fixes #97572

nit: I'd slightly prefer to do this after executing the background task - that way, if we ever need to wait for it to finish in a test we can just flush the snapshot pool queue once the listener completes.

AIUI this is a single (large) batched delete on S3 and GCS but it's 1000 API calls each time on Azure which seems a bit daft, especially now that with this change we'll be deleting mostly the same blobs concurrently. I don't see an easy way to avoid all that mostly-unnecessary work but could you open an issue to clean that up?

reply.body: I thought the same reading this code again today :) I have an idea for a rather simple fix I think, I'll open a PR shortly !

Ah sorry I parsed this wrong, normally `newGen` is just `expectedGen+1` so we are just deleting `expectedGen-1` and `expectedGen`. In theory we should only need to delete `expectedGen` but I think we can cope with one extra API call each time round.
Ah right ... 🤦 yea that's fine then :)

timeline.body: Looks good to me; I haven't dug around for tests that this might break. Left a couple of comments.

timeline.author: Armin Braun

timeline.body: Is that true any more? I think we delete all blobs up to (but not including) `newGen`.
